newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Nail buys Independent Sowetan stake.
newsitem.headline: Nail buys Independent Sowetan stake.

text.p: Black investment company New Africa Investments Ltd said on Wednesday it would buy Independent Newspaper Holdings Ltd's 42.5 percent stake in the Sowetan newspaper for 63.1 million rand.
Nail deputy chairman Dikgang Moseneke told a news conference that the deal valued the Sowetan newspaper at 150 million rand.
The effective date of the acquisition is July 1 1997, but the implementation date of the deal would be September 30, which coincides with Nail's year-end, he said.
Nail chairman Ntatho Motlana said it was also investigating setting up a joint venture newspaper distribution company with Times Media Ltd and Independent Newspapers.
The envisaged company would have a strong black empowerment element with two thirds of the shares held by black-controlled companies.

"We look forward to exploring other publishing developments with Independent and we are already looking at a major one on distribution which will involve black-control in an area dominated until now by the big publishing houses," Motlana said.
The Sowetan is South Africa's largest circulation daily newspaper.
It was unbundled by the Argus -- now Independent Newspapers -- in 1994, with Nail taking a controlling interest at the time.
Wednesday's acquisition of Independent's stake now gives Nail 100 percent ownership of the paper.
